A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMDR work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables throughout. Both end with references; neither contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: v4 reports original image-generation experiments, component ablations and ImageNet quality/diversity results, including Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds SD3-Medium diversity comparisons and reward-weight sensitivity results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The operational pipeline retains static reward weighting, DynaDG, DynaRS and subsequent joint DMD+RL optimization. The revised mathematical characterization and newly specified normalization do not establish a different implemented training procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained: t2i-2M, ShareGPT-4o-Image, GenEval, DPG Bench and ImageNet. The added diversity analysis uses the existing text-to-image setting, without introducing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: New Table 7 includes DMD and a comparator labeled DMD + PSO in the SD3-Medium diversity comparison, alongside Base-Model, DMD2 and Base + ReFL. v4's SD3-Medium benchmark comparison has no PSO comparator; its DMD2-PSO entry is under SDXL. Existing comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Tables 7–8 introduce LPIPS as a diversity metric for SD3-Medium comparisons and reward-weight analysis. The existing Section 3 protocol remains unchanged. The new LPIPS evaluation does not specify its sampling or aggregation procedure.

E4.justification: Section 4 extends the existing diversity investigation with text-to-image comparisons across methods and LPIPS sensitivity to reward weights 0.1, 0.5 and 1. This supplements the retained ImageNet diversity analysis and earlier reward-weight ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their values; Tables 7–8 add HPS and LPIPS entries. Table 8 reports LPIPS decreasing from 0.5602 to 0.5266 as the reward weight increases from 0.1 to 1. Its corresponding HPS values, 30.4024 and 32.4786, differ from unchanged Table 5c's 31.6565 and 32.8982 without an explained setting difference. These are new entries, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation 4 replaces KL against a reward-scaled teacher density with a reward-weighted KL/log-density-ratio expression. This revises the formal characterization of the already-described weighting mechanism. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: mutually beneficial DMD/RL integration, the two-stage framework, broad compatibility and few-step performance surpassing the teacher.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 now explains RT-DM through larger gradients in high-reward regions instead of explicitly targeting a reward-scaled teacher distribution. Section 4 adds that DMD regularization cannot eliminate RL's diversity cost and explains how the reward weight controls this trade-off, refining v4's more general discussion.

D1.justification: Section 2.4 specifies exponential reward weighting with beta equal to the current minibatch's maximum reward. Conversely, Section 4 removes the explicit statement that SiT uses a representation-alignment pretrained checkpoint, while retaining the citations. These change documented implementation information without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: v5 adds Zhang et al.'s 2018 perceptual-metric paper to support LPIPS. The related-work discussion and research positioning otherwise remain unchanged; subsequent references are renumbered.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to the RT-DM explanation and limitations discussion, with additional equation exposition and an affiliation marker for the first author. The section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds Tables 7–8, relocates Table 1, fits the abstract onto the first page and adjusts float placement. The dynamic-strategy analysis and DynaDG illustration exchange Figure 6/7 labels without changing their evidence.

improvement.justification: The added text-to-image diversity evidence makes an existing limitation more relevant to the main task, while explicit reward normalization improves reproducibility. These provide a modest net benefit despite incomplete LPIPS evaluation details, lost SiT initialization wording and unexplained HPS discrepancies between Tables 5c and 8. The main results and central claims remain unchanged.
